overclaims: Audited source figures do not make this cross-company calculation an audited comparison.
Support is limited to the unadjusted operating-expense-to-revenue comparison.
checks.note: Payload excerpts are cut to single words: e1 shows "expenses" and e2 shows "cost", not the full frozen sentences. The $12.65B Anthropic opex behind the ~$2.75 ratio comes from a paragraph not in the e2 context. Visible Reuters text gives only nearly $4.6B revenue and an operating loss of more than $8B. Reuters' figure excludes writedowns, so calling the comparison "unadjusted" is questionable. "Audited source figures" treats Anthropic's S-1 numbers as audited, which the evidence does not show (audited: null).

The rationale sentence "The preceding week's market observation is incomplete and outside the target date" relies on the bondfish source, which was not used and is not an evidence item, so readers cannot check it. The limitation about weekly and October prices also points to unpublished sources. The e1 excerpt "June 1, 2030." is cut from "The Notes will have a maturity date of June 1, 2030." Outcome, conditions and proposition are fine.

The proposition "Most AI data center debt deals will not be repaid" drops "these", which widens a claim about the deals referenced in the post to all AI data center debt. It also states as fact what the speaker framed as a belief ("I do not think"). The e1 excerpt "purchase and deployment" is cut from the full frozen sentence. Rationale, unresolved outcome and open horizon are consistent with the case.

overclaims: The research shows that even gigawatt-scale plans span durations around and below two years.
checks.note: The e1 explanation says Epoch's timelines span "around and below two years". Epoch reports 1 to 3.6 years from construction start to 1 GW, so the explanation leaves out durations well above two years and leans against the claim. Rationale, limitations, excerpts, dates and relations are otherwise accurate, and the unresolved outcome matches the reviews.
